summary: Batching defaults dashboards missing tier breakdown (tier dimension not appearing in panels)
description:
Issue summary
- Several panels in the "Batching Defaults – Tiered SLO" Grafana dashboard are not showing a breakdown by tier (fast/standard/cost-efficient).
- The dashboard dropdown/filter for tier is either missing or present but does not affect panel queries.
- This blocks rollout validation, since canary checks require comparing p95/p99 by tier.

Impact
- Internal: SRE + Runtime cannot validate tiered batching canary using the agreed per-tier views.
- Risk: We may miss fast-tier tail regressions (p99) or cost-efficient queue growth if tier is not visible.

Observed behavior
- Panels affected (examples):
  1) "Request latency (p95/p99)" shows only aggregate across all tiers.
  2) "Queue depth" shows aggregate; no tier legend.
  3) "Batch size distribution" legend shows model/region, but tier is missing.
- Some panels *do* show tier correctly (e.g., "Profile selection reason codes"), suggesting tier is present in some metrics but not consistently wired.

Expected behavior
- All tiered batching dashboards should support breakdown and filtering by tier using a consistent label, with legends including tier.

Steps to reproduce
1) Open Grafana: Observability → Dashboards → "Batching Defaults – Tiered SLO" (folder: Serving Runtime).
2) Set time range to last 1h.
3) Set variables: region=us-east, model_family=llama, route=*.
4) Attempt to filter by tier (fast vs standard).

Actual: No tier variable OR variable exists but panels do not change; legends show no tier.

Notes / suspected cause
- Runtime metrics recently added tier labels + cardinality controls.
- Hypothesis: dashboard queries still reference an old label key (e.g., "tier"), while metrics now emit "batching_tier" (or vice-versa), OR the label is dropped in some metric series due to cardinality limiting.

Links
- Slack context: #eng-sre "Alerting for tiered latency" and #incidents "metrics cardinality spike after canary".
- Spec: batching-defaults-observability-dashboard-spec (Confluence).

Requested outcome
- Update observability-pack dashboard JSON to use the correct tier label and ensure tier variable is present.
- Validate in prod (and staging if available) that tier breakdown appears for latency, queue depth, and batch size panels.
- Confirm the fix is compatible with metric cardinality controls (no re-introduction of high-card labels).
comments: 2026-02-20 (Aisha Bello): Noticed during canary review: tier dimension missing on top latency panels. We can’t compare fast vs standard p99 right now. Please prioritize ahead of next expansion gate.

2026-02-20 (Caleb Johnson): Taking. Initial check: metrics in Mimir show label key is batching_tier for redwood_runtime_request_latency_ms_bucket, but dashboard panels are using tier. Will patch observability-pack queries + variables.

2026-02-21 (Caleb Johnson): Confirmed inconsistency: some panels reference tier, others batching_tier. Also a few panels were aggregating with `sum without (tier)` which effectively removes the dimension. Will correct to preserve batching_tier and update legend format.
2026-02-21 (Allison Grant): Please verify we’re not re-adding any of the high-card labels we intentionally dropped in the cardinality hotfix (tenant_id, raw_route). Tier is allowed and should remain.

2026-02-22 (Caleb Johnson): PR up in observability-pack to (1) rename variable to batching_tier, (2) map default = all, (3) update affected PromQL queries and legends. Also added a note in dashboard description about expected label keys. Rolling to staging first.

2026-02-23 (Felix Schneider): Reviewed staging screenshot—tier split shows as expected on latency + batch size. Legends: `tier=fast` etc looks good. One panel (queue depth) still missing tier; query uses a different metric name. Please update that one too.
2026-02-23 (Caleb Johnson): Fixed queue depth panel: metric is redwood_scheduler_queue_depth and label key is batching_tier there as well; dashboard was using tier + a join. Updated and re-imported.
2026-02-24 (Aisha Bello): Verified in prod (us-east) for canary routes: tier dropdown present; switching fast vs standard changes p99 line; legends include batching_tier. Marking resolved.
resolution: Updated observability-pack dashboard queries/variables to use the canonical `batching_tier` label and removed aggregations that accidentally dropped the tier dimension. Validated in staging then prod that latency, queue depth, and batch size panels show tier breakdown and respond to tier filter. No high-card labels reintroduced; aligns with cardinality control changes.
